text: Okay, let's be real about this. A guy who cooks, cleans, has a job, and communicates, that's not a top-tier man. That's just a normal adult. I know a whole bunch of guys who live alone, take care of themselves, cook their own meals, and handle their responsibilities. That's an average adulthood, not some extraordinary level. Top-tier? That's a billionaire, a president, a CEO of a global company. That's a man who carries responsibility for thousands of people, runs businesses, solves massive problems, and on top of that, still manages his personal life. So when women try to call cooking and cleaning top-tier, that's manipulation and twisting of the definition. And here's how easy it is to flip. Imagine if I said, an extraordinary woman is just an average man. She supports you when you need it, understands you, can have deep conversations, but also jokes around, does not nag you, and plays video games with you. Do you know how many women are like that? Almost none. Meanwhile, most of my guy friends are exactly like this. That's how this trick works. You take ordinary qualities from one side, call them extraordinary, and pretend you've proven something. Guys, don't get baited by the manipulations that some women use. And women, come on, stop hating on men. And stop it with these manipulations. Ladies, you don't need to put men down to advance feminism. And men, we don't need to put women down to advance masculine ideas.
